details: The Federal Reserve maintained the federal funds rate at 3.5%-3.75% on July 29, 2026, for the fifth consecutive meeting. However, three officials dissented, advocating for a 25 basis point hike due to persistent inflation exceeding the 2% target, largely driven by energy market supply shocks. Despite the hold, this hawkish split suggests continued uncertainty and the potential for future rate increases if inflation remains elevated. Crypto markets, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, showed minimal immediate reaction to the announcement.
title: Fed Holds Rates Steady, Hawkish Dissent Fuels Future Hike Concerns

details: The U.S. Senate has postponed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a crucial piece of legislation aimed at providing regulatory clarity for the cryptocurrency market. This delay is viewed as a significant setback for institutional adoption of digital assets, as it removes a potential catalyst for increased investment and prolongs regulatory uncertainty. JPMorgan reportedly believes the fading prospects of such a bill negatively impact the outlook for the crypto sector.
title: US Senate Delays CLARITY Act, Slowing Institutional Crypto Adoption

details: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index decreased by 0.1% month-over-month in June 2026, and the core PCE index, which excludes volatile food and energy components, increased by 0.1%. Both figures were in line with market expectations. On an annual basis, headline PCE inflation eased to 3.7% from 4.1%, and core PCE softened to 3.3% from 3.4%. This moderation in a key inflation gauge could alleviate some pressure on the Federal Reserve regarding future interest rate decisions.
title: US PCE Price Index Falls, Core PCE Cools in June

details: A recent Wintermute report highlights a significant shift in the crypto market, with institutional investors now occupying a central role in trading. These institutions accounted for 72% of over-the-counter (OTC) trading volume in the first half of 2026. This increased institutional participation is reportedly leading to a reduction in Bitcoin's realized volatility, which fell from approximately 70% in previous cycles to nearly 45% in the current cycle. Furthermore, capital is becoming more concentrated on a smaller number of cryptocurrencies, while tokenized assets, particularly favored by institutions, have grown to $31 billion.
title: Institutional Investors Drive Crypto Market, Reducing Volatility
